topic: Claude Code deleted 15% of a heritage archive: blast radius and the case for controlling where your agent runs
title: Claude Code went rogue and deleted years of work
description: Working value; the package stage overwrites the final ones in its own note.
hook_candidates: A Bengaluru heritage project let an AI agent work beside a decade of stone scans.
You let a coding agent run shell commands where your real work lives.
For four minutes, a man watched an AI delete his life's work.
An AI agent tried to stop itself. Its safety system said no. Twice.
Fifteen percent of a decade, gone in four minutes.
The agent was safe. The archive was not.
You trust the sandbox. The sandbox has cracks.
Guardrails did not save this archive. Backups did.
One stray quote mark deleted a heritage archive.
Keep the agent. Shrink its reach.
narration_full: A Bengaluru heritage project let an AI agent work beside a decade of scans. Here's what broke. Udaya Kumar P L is the project's honorary director. For four minutes he watched an AI agent delete his files. The agent noticed and tried to kill the process. The safety layer blocked the rescue, then blocked it again. He shut the computer down himself. The loss was fifteen percent of the project's records. Not code. Original photographs of inscriptions, hero stones, temples, and coins. Urbanisation is erasing those stones, so the scans, detailed digital models, were irreplaceable. Each commercial scanner cost more than twenty-five thousand dollars. Name what changed: the command. A quoting error, one stray quote mark that turns words into a command, rewrote a cache-clearing chore into delete everything. Then the asking changed. The agent was Claude Code, Anthropic's tool that runs shell commands, typed orders the computer obeys. Answer yes, don't ask again, and the approval saves permanently to the project. What never changed was the reach. The agent worked where the archive lived. The risk was never intelligence; it was blast radius, everything a failing agent can reach. Inside a sandbox, an isolated environment, the same bug deletes only the sandbox. Name what survived: the backup. The copy on network-attached storage, a separate box on the network, came through untouched. The copy on his computer's drive did not. The agent could not reach the box, so the box could not burn. Do not mistake this for a cloud story. The same agent with full permissions on your desk deletes just as thoroughly. The report says the agent breached even the sandboxed environment. And it says no human at Anthropic has answered him. The project's answer is more copies, kept farther away. A second storage box the agent cannot write to, and offsite tape. The control is isolation plus tested backups: storage the agent cannot write, ask-before-shell permissions, a sandbox, one restore test. First, move the irreplaceable to a box the agent cannot write. Second, set permissions to ask before every shell command, and delete saved approvals. Third, run the agent in a sandbox with only the project folder, then test one restore. Ask-permissions interrupt your flow. Isolation takes setup and slows the loop. Fifteen percent of the records are gone for good. The rest survived on a box the agent could not touch. The fix was never a smarter agent; it was a shorter reach.

analogy.vehicle: the blast circle (a red circle scaling out from an agent dot until it swallows the archive)
analogy.mapping: blast radius as physical reach: the risk is everything the agent can touch, and the fix is shortening the reach, not making the agent smarter
analogy.limit: a circle implies a clean boundary; the report says the sandbox boundary itself was breached, so the picture holds only as the control you design, not one you inherit

notes_for_review: The sandbox breach and Anthropic's silence are both attributed to the report in scene eight. Spoken numbers capped at three. The first/second/third labels are the viewer's own steps (has_process brief). The trade-off sentences are the judge's graft from draft B.
